positions.position: P0 — the invariant 'reader shift equals writer shift' is no longer expressible; a future change to the core constant would silently corrupt reads of old indexes with no compile-time warning.
P1 — silent-drift hazard worth fixing by stating the invariant in one place or commenting the duplication.
P1 — gratuitous duplication that future maintainers will diverge unless the decoupling intent is documented.
P1 — two copies of the same magic number drift; give it one home or annotate the equality requirement.
Not raised as a duplication issue (focused instead on duplicated NAME identity across modules).

dissents.topic: Severity of NAME / API visibility downgrade (public to package-private)

positions.position: P0 — public static final NAME constants and protected fields on a public abstract class are silently narrowed; downstream consumers (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, custom codecs) will fail to compile.
P2 — behavior-altering API narrowing dressed as a refactor; audit external use before merging but not necessarily a blocker.
P2 — small but real break of the protected contract in a backward-compat module; pick a consistent altitude (keep protected or make class non-public).
P1 — abstraction leak: the test package now depends on package-private internals of a frozen legacy format.
P2 — fine in context given @lucene.experimental and the move to backward_codecs, worth a one-line confirmation no external subclasses existed.
P1 — quietly tightened subclassing precondition without a stated rationale; restore protected or seal the class.

dissents.topic: Severity of fieldsWriter throwing UnsupportedOperationException vs. lifting read-only into the type system

positions.position: P1 LSP violation — the supertype promises a usable writer; a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat marker or supportsWriting() predicate should lift the restriction into the type system.
P1 — papering over read/write complecting; a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat split would express the actual fact.
P1 — a smuggled goto out of a method whose declared contract is to return a writer; failure should be at codec/IndexWriter construction, not first flush.
P2 — consistent with established backward_codecs pattern; acceptable accumulated smell.
P2 — needs a literate class-level comment stating the invariant rather than a structural change.
Did not flag the UOE pattern itself directly; focused on the missing @Deprecated and silent narrowing.
P0 — removing @Deprecated while disabling writes at runtime leaves users with no compile-time warning before the runtime exception.
P1 — deprecation signal lost at exactly the lifecycle moment it carries the most information for migrating users.
P2 — restore @Deprecated so 'this is legacy' travels with the type as a tool-checkable signal.
Not flagged.

dissents.topic: Whether the patch should land at all in current form

positions.position: NEEDS-WORK — split into mechanical-move, API-deprecation, and writer-disable patches; the PR description openly admits the work is incomplete (scorer left behind in core).
Merge-ready after a quick decision on the constant duplication; the data shape is right.
Mechanically sound; needs literate comments but not a blocker.
Reasoned enough to move but tested-not-proved on the read-only invariant; unstated preconditions need to be mechanically enforced before merge.
Does not block correctness for read-only back-compat, but the read-only-after-rotation policy should become a written contract before this pattern is repeated.
Right direction; the remaining complecting and NAME-identity duplication are worth a second look before merging.

issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT duplicated rather than referenced from canonical source — invariant that reader shift equals writer shift no longer expressible
issues.detail: The original code referenced Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT via static import. The move introduces a new constant Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16 in the backward_codecs package. There is no compile-time or runtime check that these two constants remain equal. If the core constant is ever changed, the legacy reader will silently mis-decode existing indexes. State the invariant in one place or annotate the duplication explicitly. Reviewers split on severity (dijkstra P0, knuth/torvalds/pike P1).

issues.description: Public API broken: NAME constants demoted from public to package-private on both legacy formats
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME were public static final String constants. External codec registries, integration tests, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and downstream consumers that reference them will fail to compile. Silently narrowing visibility in the same patch that moves the class is the wrong shape — either keep public with @Deprecated or remove with explicit migration notes. Knuth treats this as P2 pending external-use audit; torvalds treats as P0 break.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation removed from both legacy formats just as writing is disabled
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat were previously @Deprecated; the diff strips the annotation. Users get a runtime UnsupportedOperationException with no compile-time warning. Moving to backward_codecs is precisely when @Deprecated is most informative for users still on the old fully-qualified name during migration. Torvalds rates P0, dijkstra P1, hickey P2.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of read-only-ness being expressed in the type system (LSP violation)
issues.detail: KnnVectorsFormat / FlatVectorsFormat supertypes promise a usable writer from fieldsWriter(); the legacy subtypes unconditionally throw. This is an LSP violation (Liskov), a complecting of read/write concerns in one type (Hickey), and a smuggled goto out of an advertised contract (Dijkstra). The right shape is a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat split, a supportsWriting() predicate, or failing at codec/IndexWriter construction. Pike notes this is consistent with existing backward_codecs precedent (P2). Knuth wants a literate javadoc paragraph rather than a structural change.

issues.description: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec parameters that are now silently discarded
issues.detail: The constructor still takes numMergeWorkers and ExecutorService mergeExec, validates them (throwing on inconsistent combinations), but the fields were removed and fieldsWriter throws anyway. Callers passing real executors will believe they configured something; they did not. The contract advertised by the signature contradicts the behavior. Either narrow the constructor to read-only parameters or document loudly that these arguments have no effect and are kept only for source compatibility.

issues.description: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields demoted from protected to package-private while class remains public abstract
issues.detail: Fields dimension, size, numBytes, scalarQuantizer, similarityFunction, vectorsScorer, compress, slice, binaryValue, byteBuffer, byteSize, lastOrd, scoreCorrectionConstant were protected and are now package-private. The class is still public abstract, so external subclasses cannot access these fields — the inheritance contract is silently tightened. Either keep them protected, make the class package-private/sealed/final, or document the audit that no out-of-tree subclasses exist. Severity split: torvalds P0, liskov/dijkstra P1, knuth/hickey/pike P2.

issues.description: Three or more concerns shipped as one patch (mechanical move, API narrowing, writer disable, test scaffolding refactor)
issues.detail: The diff conflates physical relocation, API visibility narrowing, writer neutralization, and RW/V0/V1 test scaffolding. Each is independently reviewable; together they obscure what is mechanical vs. semantic. Author also openly states in the PR description the work is incomplete (scorer not movable yet). THREE-PATCHES — split into mechanical-move, API-deprecation, and writer-disable patches.

issues.description: PR description openly states the work is incomplete (scorer left in core, additional things to figure out)
issues.detail: Author writes 'I have most of the logic moved, but there are additional things to figure out' and 'I don't think we can easily move Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer just yet.' That is a draft, not a patch ready to land. Resolve the scorer location before merging or scope the diff to only the parts that are actually complete.

issues.description: Writer logic moved into test tree creates a load-bearing test-only writer class
issues.detail: Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter moved to backward-codecs src/test means the only path to write the legacy format now lives in test source. If bw-compat index generation tooling or any non-test consumer needs to produce legacy indexes, they cannot. State explicitly whether bw-compat index generation lives in tests; if not, this is the wrong shape.

issues.description: Test-only RW subclasses use inheritance to override fieldsWriter and re-enable writing, abusing subtyping
issues.detail: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99RWV1HnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat extend the legacy read-only formats solely to override fieldsWriter and put writing back. This is inheritance-for-reuse working around the supertype's stated invariant ('Old codecs may only be used for reading'). Composition through a writer factory using package-private constructors of the writer class would honor the contract without subclassing a type whose contract forbids writing.

issues.description: rawVectorFormat field visibility widened from private to package-private to serve test-tree writer subclass
issues.detail: Production code's encapsulation was loosened so Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat (in the test tree) can read it. Coupling between production and test code is invisible from the production class. Either inject the raw format via a constructor or protected accessor with a documented contract, or accept that this class is now part of the testable surface and document the load-bearing widening.

issues.description: Wrong module boundary: backward_codecs still imports core lucene99 classes (Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat/Reader, Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat)
issues.detail: Moving Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat into backward_codecs while it still imports Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat, Lucene99HnswVectorsReader, and Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat from core tethers the legacy read path to whatever core's lucene99 looks like over time. The backward-codecs contract is read-only isolation; a future core refactor will silently break legacy reads unless the boundary is drawn cleanly.

issues.description: On-disk NAME 'Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat' temporarily duplicated between backward_codecs and core during transition
issues.detail: The rename moves these classes to backward_codecs but keeps the same static NAME string. Until the originals under lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/codecs/lucene99 are fully removed and SPI registrations cleaned, two classes identify themselves with the same on-disk name. The on-disk name is a value identifying the format and must have exactly one owning class at a time. Verify the core copies are deleted in the same commit.

issues.description: SPI registers a non-writeable format — fail-fast moved from load time to first flush
issues.detail: module-info.java and META-INF/services register Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat as KnnVectorsFormat providers. A user can construct an IndexWriter against a Codec resolving to these formats and the failure only surfaces at the first segment flush — potentially after substantial work. Detect 'read-only format selected as writer' at codec construction or IndexWriter init instead.

issues.description: Reader-only legacy formats lack a literate class-level comment stating the read-only invariant
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat have fieldsWriter throwing UnsupportedOperationException('Old codecs may only be used for reading') with no class-level javadoc explaining the invariant. A reader picking this up cold has to infer the regime from a single thrown exception. Add a literate paragraph at the class javadoc explaining the retention rationale, where writes now live, and the test-only writer location.

issues.description: Two RW test formats (V0 and V1) with overlapping names lack documentation of what each version means on disk
issues.detail: Lucene99RWHnswScalarQuantizationVectorsFormat is renamed to V0, and a new V1 is added. The version suffix carries on-disk semantics that aren't documented centrally — only a one-line javadoc hint deep in an inner class. A package-info paragraph or README in the test package explaining V0 = pre-bits, V1 = post-bits (VERSION_ADD_BITS) would prevent the next contributor from adding V2 without understanding the shape. Hickey adds a structural angle: this encodes version-as-class-identity instead of version-as-value.

issues.description: VERSION_START / VERSION_ADD_BITS / VERSION_CURRENT lack on-disk semantics comments
issues.detail: The format keeps VERSION_START = 0, VERSION_ADD_BITS = 1, VERSION_CURRENT = VERSION_ADD_BITS as bare integers. For a legacy format whose purpose is to be read correctly across versions, what each transition changed on disk should be stated next to the constants so an engineer debugging a corrupted segment isn't forced into git archaeology.

issues.description: Read-only-after-rotation policy missing as a documented invariant or marker type
issues.detail: The contract 'Old codecs may only be used for reading' is communicated only by UnsupportedOperationException strings on two classes. For a multi-team, multi-year codebase, the read-only policy should be a written contract (javadoc on a base class, marker interface, or module-level doc) so future codec authors don't have to re-derive it. Consider a ReadOnlyVectorsFormat marker if this pattern repeats with future rotations.

issues.description: PR commit message hedges and does not explain the scorer migration story
issues.detail: CHANGES.txt entry is fine, but the PR description doesn't tell a future maintainer why the scorer is stuck behind in core, what the migration story is for users who set Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat on their codec config, or how reads of legacy segments get scored without the original scorer being movable.

issues.description: Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat default constructor is 'protected' on a non-abstract class with no documented subclassing contract
issues.detail: The new test-only Lucene99RWScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat declares a protected sole constructor on a public, non-abstract class with no abstract methods, no documented extension point, and no other subclass in the diff. Either make the class abstract and document what subclasses must do, or make the constructor package-private/public to match its actual use. Sloppy modifiers accumulate unstated preconditions.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a physical move of Lucene99 scalar-quantized vector formats into backward_codecs with writers neutralized via UnsupportedOperationException and test-only RW/V0/V1 subclasses re-providing write paths for round-trip tests. The strongest cross-panel claims are: (1) DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT was silently duplicated rather than referenced from the canonical Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat constant (flagged by knuth, hickey-implicitly, torvalds, pike, dijkstra — dijkstra rates P0 as a real on-disk-corruption hazard); (2) the read-only constraint is enforced by runtime UOE in a method whose type signature still advertises a writer, an LSP violation and complecting that should be lifted into the type system or fail at codec construction (liskov, hickey, dijkstra, with pike/knuth dissenting on whether structural change is required); and (3) API surface was silently narrowed in the same patch (NAME public→package-private, OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues protected fields→package-private, @Deprecated stripped, numMergeWorkers/mergeExec accepted-and-discarded). The strongest preserved disagreement is between Torvalds (NEEDS-WORK, split into three patches, multiple P0s, author admits incompleteness) and Pike (merge-ready after one minor decision on the constant duplication); Hickey, Liskov, Dijkstra, and Knuth sit between these poles, treating the work as directionally right but structurally unfinished — particularly around making the read-only-after-rotation policy a written, tool-checkable contract rather than a runtime exception and a stripped annotation.
